summary: Close Task 107 repository architecture validation drift by registering existing PostgreSQL adapters, aligning storefront provider families with validated Connector SDK manifests, and keeping registered frontend and n8n package-manager dependencies outside the first-party Go inventory.

impacts.evidence: The cleanup changes repository inventory metadata and validation traversal only; tenant scope and RLS behavior are unchanged.
No persisted or public personal field is added; frontend dependency material remains local and excluded from first-party source classification.
No OpenAPI operation, request, response, status code or authorization permission changes.
No event name, envelope, producer or consumer behavior changes.
Provider policy now recognizes the existing Connector SDK storefront family already declared by the three validated manifests.
Catalog image and report repositories are existing adapters; registration adds no SQL or migration.
Only the explicit frontend and n8n package-manager dependency roots are skipped; vendor and symlink checks remain fail-closed everywhere else and are regression-tested.
Capability risk classification and approval-required remote writes are unchanged.
No audit record, lineage record or SIEM export behavior changes.
Sync execution, reconciliation state and idempotency behavior are unchanged.
No webhook destination, signature, replay or egress behavior changes.
The canonical architecture gate can now report a clean result instead of known inventory false positives.
Rollback restores validation metadata only; no runtime or persisted business state requires conversion.
Architecture tests cover both bounded package-manager dependency-root exclusions while existing hidden vendor and symlink rejection tests remain active.
